label: UniFi Dream Machine Beast
description: UniFi Dream Machine Beast (UDM-Beast) - 2x 1G RJ45 + 8x 10G RJ45 + 2x 10G SFP+ (10G/1G) + 2x 25G SFP28 (25G/10G/1G) + 1x console. 100 W max.
notes:
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-beast (HTTP 200, 679,909 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = (1) Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 3A Max., 50/60 Hz (1) USP-RPS DC input, 11.5V DC, 13.05A"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so eth0 / eth1 / eth2 / eth3 / eth4 / eth5 / eth6 / eth7 / eth8 / eth9 now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

Port census re-read from the vendor's own Port Layout table: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-beast (HTTP 200, 679,909 B, server-rendered, read 2026-11-19 21:5x UTC). The table prints five rows verbatim: "1 GbE RJ45 = 2 (1G/100M/10M)", "10 GbE RJ45 = 8 (10G/5G/2.5G/1G/100M)", "10G SFP+ = 2 (10G/1G)", "25G SFP28 = 2 (25G/10G/1G)", and "Console = 1". Four of them were already modelled (eth0-eth1, eth2-eth9, sfp1-sfp2, sfp3-sfp4); the fifth was not, and the two 1 GbE rows also print a 10M rung this spec did not carry. Both corrected here: the console socket is now an interface, and eth0/eth1 advertise 1G/100M/10M. The same table prints "Max. WAN Port Count = 8" and "Default WAN Ports = (1) 25G SFP28 / (1) 10 GbE RJ45"; those two default uplinks are documented in prose rather than pinned as port roles, so no saved lab has its WAN assumption moved underneath it. No PoE row appears anywhere on the page, so nothing here sources power and every copper port keeps poeIn: false.
